od_032_position: OD-032 is PENDING and is the only withheld limb in this slice. Its exact question is which lifecycle owner and canonical identifier namespace 011 DOMAIN_MODEL.md assigns to the lifecycle-bearing records DM-REQ-001 does not name -- ScoreSnapshot, Check Result, Session, LegalHold, LifecycleDeletionJob, Notification, Delivery, Parsed Artifact, Index Receipt and Issue Set -- and, separately, which bounded context owns LegalHold, since 016 STATE_MODEL.md names a `Security Context` that 011 does not define. Its Safe Interim Behavior is exact: no record is added to DM-REQ-001, no namespace or lifecycle owner is inferred for an unassigned record, no implementation may invent either, Volume I's existing logical field names and behavioural contracts for these records are unchanged and remain authoritative FOR BEHAVIOUR, an assignment 016 already names stands and is not reopened, and any Volume II or persistence artifact that REQUIRES a canonical namespace for an unassigned record remains blocked rather than choosing one. Blocking Impact records: Volume II -- no for behaviour, yes for any artifact requiring a canonical namespace; implementation -- no under the interim; production -- no; feature -- no. The withheld limb at S-11 is therefore exactly: a canonical identifier namespace or lifecycle owner declared for LegalHold or Check Result, and a bounded-context assignment for LegalHold. EVIDENCE IS NOT AFFECTED: OD-032's own text records that 011 DOMAIN_MODEL.md already admits Evidence as a lifecycle-bearing auxiliary record with owner Evidence Context and namespace `evd_id`, and cites that as the precedent the pending decision would follow. Every behavioural limb of CAP-013 and PRULE-016 -- fields, digest, provenance, validation authority and transitions, classification, immutability, tenant integrity, retention split, expiry, hold, destruction and propagation -- is contracted in full. The limb is isolated on MTX-013 only; MTX-067 requires no namespace for an unassigned record and withholds nothing.
settled_decisions_position: OD-011 is RESOLVED (Option 1 -- `retention-interim-v1` is the fixed Volume I retention baseline). OD-029 is RESOLVED (Option 2 -- WF-007 produces `EvidenceRetentionExpiring` with the integrity-validation service as the named authority). OD-030 is RESOLVED (Option 3 -- retention-expiry destruction of an already-`invalid` payload is proved by a distinct immutable `security_audit` deletion audit record, stays on the existing capture cursor and 24-month maximum rather than accelerating to the accrued minimum, and appends no Evidence Validation Decision). All three are settled authority and are implemented as ratified; none withholds anything here. OD-031 is pending but its Affected Acceptance Criteria are AC-CAP-025, AC-WF-013 and AC-PRULE-042 -- routine 7-year `product_history`, `identity_commercial` and `security_audit` destruction owned by CAP-025 and WF-013 in S-23 -- and it withholds nothing at S-11.

MTX-013.interface_type: Evidence creation is producer-driven and has no command of its own: each producer-enabled `evidence_type` is created by the workflow that observes it. The principal-reachable surface is exactly the Evidence Validation Decision command, plus the read paths the visibility contract governs. CAP-013's Actor is the tenant-scoped integrity-validation service, with a SecurityOperator holding protected `evidence.validation.manage` in authorized security or legal scope.
MTX-013.route: Not applicable - Volume I defines the actors, the permissions and the command envelope but no HTTP path, method or transport. Transport exposure is owned by API_CONTRACTS.md at the Volume II baseline. There is no Evidence-creation endpoint: creating Evidence out of band would bypass the producer contract that binds each type to its observing workflow.
MTX-013.request_schema: Validation Decision command: Evidence ID, prior effective status, expected validation-state version, resulting status, enumerated reason, policy version, authority, idempotency key, correlation ID. Evidence creation input, per producer: raw observations or immutable references, digest, same-Organization lineage, schema and collector versions, Evidence Classification, validation result, and the Evidence Payload `payload_retention_class`, per CAP-013 Inputs.
MTX-013.response_schema: Valid, invalid or quarantined Evidence with immutable provenance and access history; the appended immutable Evidence Validation Decision; and, when current support ceases to be valid, the atomic unavailable score and suppressed-Recommendation projection, per CAP-013 Outputs.
MTX-013.controller: Not applicable - no HTTP adapter is defined by Volume I; see route.
MTX-013.command: `Workflows::Wf007::SubmitEvidenceValidationDecision` (the only principal-reachable path), `Workflows::Wf007::EmitEvidenceRetentionExpiring` (the OD-029 scheduled path under integrity-validation service authority), `Workflows::Wf007::DestroyExpiredEvidencePayload` (the OD-030 path). Evidence creation itself is performed by the producing workflow -- WF-003 for `verification_observation`, WF-005 for `source_document` and `crawl_observation`, WF-006 for `parsed_content` and `external_measurement` -- and CAP-013 contributes the envelope contract those producers MUST satisfy rather than a creation command of its own.
MTX-013.command_input: The Decision command names Evidence, prior effective status, expected validation-state version, resulting status, enumerated reason, policy version, authority, idempotency key and correlation ID. A stale version, a same-status request, or an unlisted transition or reason is rejected WITHOUT a Decision.
MTX-013.command_output: One immutable Evidence Validation Decision containing decision ID, Evidence ID, prior and resulting effective status, reason code, authority, policy version, `decided_at_utc`, state version and correlation ID; plus every applicable propagation effect committed in the same transaction.
MTX-013.actor: Tenant-scoped integrity-validation service for every allowed transition and reason. A SecurityOperator holding protected `evidence.validation.manage` in active incident, adjudication or support scope may submit ONLY `valid -> quarantined` and only for `security_restriction`, `consent_review` or `retention_review`. Neither may mutate Evidence bytes or an earlier Decision. No other actor may change Evidence validation state.
MTX-013.organization_scope: The Evidence's Organization. Referenced Organization, Project, Source and Evaluation records MUST all belong to it.
MTX-013.aggregate: Evidence as a lifecycle-bearing auxiliary record with owner Evidence Context and namespace `evd_id`, per 011 DOMAIN_MODEL.md's accepted admission; EvidenceValidationDecision as its immutable append-only history; EvidencePayload as the referenced immutable bytes. Issue, CheckResult, ScoreSnapshot, RecommendationArtifact, Citation and CurrentScoreProjection are propagation targets owned by other slices.
MTX-013.aggregate_boundary: A transition away from `valid` is a deliberately WIDE atomic commit and Volume I says so: before the Decision commits, the same transaction performs every applicable current effect. That is the whole point of the rule -- a narrow commit would leave a window in which a current read returns a numeric score supported by Evidence the system has already decided is not valid.
MTX-013.value_objects: EvidenceId, SchemaVersion, EvidenceType, PayloadReference, ContentSha256, CapturedAtUtc, ObservedAtUtc, SourceSystem, CollectionMethod, CollectorVersion, ValidationStatus, ValidationReasonCode, DataClassification, PayloadRetentionClass, CorrelationId, EvidenceValidationDecisionId, DecidedAtUtc, EvidenceProvenance, EvidenceSource (a conceptual view, never a persisted field).
MTX-013.domain_service: The tenant-scoped integrity-validation service is named by Volume I and is the sole authority for `quarantined -> valid`, for every transition to `invalid`, and for the full reason set on `valid -> quarantined`. It is not a convenience object: its identity is the authority recorded on each Decision.
MTX-013.repository: `EvidenceRepository`, `EvidenceValidationDecisionRepository`, `EvidencePayloadRepository`, `LegalHoldRepository` read-only at the hold checkpoint, `CurrentScoreProjectionRepository` and `RecommendationArtifactRepository` at the propagation boundary, `CitationRepository` at the propagation boundary.
MTX-013.persistence_model: `evidence` carries every required attribute with `validation_status` as the immutable CREATION-TIME decision; the retained bytes, content digest, tenant references, provenance fields and classification are immutable after creation, so a corrected observation is a NEW Evidence record rather than an update. `evidence_validation_decisions` is append-only and is the authority for effective status; no same-status Decision is created and `invalid` is terminal. Evidence Source is a conceptual origin view over `source_system` and applicable `source_id` and MUST NOT be persisted as a separate field, entity or type literal. `payload_retention_class` classifies ONLY the referenced Evidence Payload; the envelope, digest, provenance, Validation Decisions and downstream lineage are always `product_history`, including after payload destruction.
MTX-013.migration: Not applicable at this row for Evidence itself - the canonical schema owns `evidence`, `evidence_validation_decisions` and the payload reference, and Evidence's namespace `evd_id` and owner Evidence Context are already admitted by 011 DOMAIN_MODEL.md. WITHHELD under OD-032 and MUST NOT be migrated: a canonical identifier namespace or lifecycle owner for LegalHold or Check Result, or a bounded-context assignment for LegalHold. Volume II is blocked on any artifact that REQUIRES one; behaviour is permitted under the interim and Volume I's existing logical field names remain authoritative for it.
MTX-013.transaction_boundary: One transaction per Decision. It atomically appends the Decision and `EvidenceValidationChanged`, updates every affected current score and Recommendation projection BEFORE commit, and enqueues idempotent recalculation. A transition away from `valid` performs every applicable current effect in that same transaction: if the Evidence supports a selected current Issue or any passed or failed Check Result supplying current pillar coverage, mark the Current Score Projection unavailable, add `invalid_evidence` to its de-duplicated fixed-precedence reason set, and suppress every published Recommendation Artifact whose origin Issue is affected; INDEPENDENTLY, suppress every published Artifact whose rationale or Citation references that Evidence. The two suppression limbs are separate predicates and neither subsumes the other.
MTX-013.concurrency: The expected validation-state version is mandatory: a stale command is rejected without a Decision, so two operators cannot both transition one Evidence record. `validation_status` is immutable at creation and effective status derives from the append-only Decision history, so a concurrent read never observes a half-applied transition. Check Results and historical snapshots retain the Validation Decision IDs and statuses frozen when they were created and never mutate, so a Decision landing concurrently with a Check persist cannot rewrite the frozen tuple. Recalculation is idempotent and is enqueued rather than run inline, so a redelivery cannot double-apply.
MTX-013.idempotency: The Decision command is idempotent by its idempotency key: exact replay returns the Decision WITHOUT repeating suppression, the event, or recalculation. A same-status request creates no Decision at all rather than a duplicate. `EvidenceRetentionExpiring` is emitted EXACTLY ONCE per Evidence Payload at its 30-day boundary; the emitted cursor is retained so a rescheduled evaluation emits no second event. Payload destruction is idempotent on the payload reference: a second destruction of already-destroyed bytes appends no second `security_audit` record.
MTX-013.background_job: `EvidenceRetentionExpiringJob` at 30 days before the current `product_evidence_payload` retention maximum; `EvidencePayloadDestructionJob` at the 24-month elapsed maximum on the capture cursor; `EvidenceRecalculationJob` for the idempotent score and Recommendation recalculation each Decision enqueues. No job may mutate Evidence bytes, an earlier Decision, or a historical snapshot.
MTX-013.queue: The evaluation and lifecycle queues, per the Volume I Background Processing action registry. Queue identity is owned by BACKGROUND_PROCESSING.md; this row does not rename it.
MTX-013.retry_policy: Not applicable as a workflow retry - CAP-013 defines none. A rejected Decision is terminal for that command: a stale version, same-status request, or unlisted transition or reason is refused and the correct recovery is a new Decision against the LATEST version, not a retry of the refused one. The recalculation the Decision enqueues is idempotent, so its own redelivery repeats no effect.
MTX-013.terminal_failure: `invalid` is terminal: no transition leaves it, and corrected content is a new Evidence record. Creation or downstream use fails for an invalid field, missing bytes, digest mismatch, unknown schema, tenant mismatch or an unknown `payload_retention_class`, and creates no record on rejection. Reserved `operator_attestation` returns `F1-DOMAIN-409 / evidence_type_unavailable` on every attempted creation; an unknown or legacy alias, including `operator_submission`, returns `F1-VALIDATION-400 / evidence_type_invalid`. No implementation may normalize an alias into a recognized type.
MTX-013.reconciliation: A later `quarantined -> valid` triggers recalculation, removes `invalid_evidence` ONLY when no selected score input has invalid Evidence, and may restore a promoted snapshot and eligible Recommendation Artifacts. No automatic republication occurs until every publication predicate passes again. Recalculation replaces the COMPLETE reason set with all and only reasons applicable to the recalculated inputs -- it does not subtract one code and leave the rest. A legal hold suspends destruction and the payload is destroyed at the first eligible instant after release.
MTX-013.domain_events: `EvidenceValidationChanged`, emitted in the same transaction as every accepted transition. `EvidenceRetentionExpiring`, which under OD-029 Option 2 has exactly one producer -- WF-007 under the integrity-validation service authority -- and is emitted once per Evidence Payload at 30 days before its current `product_evidence_payload` retention maximum. Under OD-030 Option 3 payload destruction emits NO domain event and appends NO Evidence Validation Decision: it is proved by exactly one immutable `security_audit` deletion audit record.
MTX-013.event_payload: `EvidenceValidationChanged`: the canonical envelope with the real `organization_id`, plus Decision ID, Evidence ID, prior and resulting effective status, reason code, authority, policy version, `decided_at_utc`, state version and correlation ID. `EvidenceRetentionExpiring`: the Evidence identity, its Organization, the capture cursor, the maximum instant and the correlation ID -- exactly those fields. Neither payload carries Evidence bytes, challenge plaintext or restricted observation content.
MTX-013.event_producer: `Workflows::Wf007` is the sole producer of both events. OD-029 makes that exclusive for `EvidenceRetentionExpiring`: no lifecycle service, no second workflow and no notification route variant produces it.
MTX-013.event_consumers: S-13 consumes `EvidenceValidationChanged` as the trigger for idempotent score recalculation; S-14 consumes it for Recommendation suppression and republication. WF-011 consumes the `EvidenceRetentionExpiring` reassessment request through the accepted path when the Project remains active. No consumer may re-decide the Decision.
MTX-013.serializer: Not applicable - no transport exposure is defined by Volume I; see route.
MTX-013.authorization_entry_point: The Decision command, before mutation, resolving the exact actor limits: the integrity-validation service for every allowed transition and reason; a SecurityOperator only for `valid -> quarantined` and only for the three permitted reasons, and only in active incident, adjudication or support scope.
MTX-013.permission_checks: `evidence.validation.manage`, whose Permission Baseline cell reads `quarantine-only in authorized security/legal scope` for a SecurityOperator and `integrity-validation service only for all allowed transitions` for the service, and deny for every other role. It is a PROTECTED grant, so it requires approval within 24 hours by a SecurityOperator other than the requester and an active expiry. `evidence.restricted.read` is a separate protected explicit grant that raises ONLY the granted OrganizationAdmin's Evidence payload access to `restricted`; it broadens no resource scope and no other field permission, and it authorizes no validation transition.
MTX-013.tenant_boundary: Validation Rule 1 is absolute: referenced Organization, Project, Source and Evaluation records MUST belong to the same Organization. A cross-Organization reference, missing referenced bytes, digest mismatch or unknown schema version MUST reject the downstream write with a data-integrity error AND an audit event. A Support Session scopes an already-permitted action to an Organization, resource and action allowlist; it is not itself a read grant and never widens a Permission Baseline cell.
MTX-013.error_contract: `F1-DOMAIN-409 / evidence_type_unavailable` for reserved `operator_attestation`. `F1-VALIDATION-400 / evidence_type_invalid` for an unknown or legacy alias including `operator_submission`. Rejection without a Decision for a stale expected validation-state version, a same-status request, or an unlisted transition or reason. Creation rejection for an invalid field, missing immutable bytes, digest mismatch, unknown schema version, tenant mismatch or an unknown `payload_retention_class`. Downstream data-integrity rejection with an audit event for a cross-Organization reference, missing referenced bytes, digest mismatch or unknown schema version. Every rejection creates no record.
MTX-013.audit_record: Every Decision with decision ID, Evidence ID, prior and resulting effective status, reason code, authority, policy version, `decided_at_utc`, state version and correlation ID. Immutable provenance and access history per CAP-013 Outputs. Under OD-030, exactly one immutable `security_audit` deletion audit record proves retention-expiry destruction of an already-`invalid` payload; the LifecycleDeletionJob and its Deletion Evidence are asserted ABSENT from that path and remain the Account-deletion and Organization-closure mechanism only.
MTX-013.observability: Evidence capture success and citation validity rates, per CAP-013 Observability Requirements. Every Decision emits `EvidenceValidationChanged`; every 30-day payload boundary emits exactly one `EvidenceRetentionExpiring`; every retention-expiry destruction writes exactly one `security_audit` record. A destruction with no audit record and a boundary with no event are both detectable.
MTX-013.retention: `retention-interim-v1` under the resolved OD-011. For every producer-enabled Evidence type in Volume I, `payload_retention_class` is exactly `product_evidence_payload` and NO caller may choose another value; an unknown class rejects Evidence creation. That field classifies ONLY the referenced Evidence Payload. The Evidence envelope, digest, provenance, Validation Decisions and downstream lineage are always `product_history`, INCLUDING AFTER PAYLOAD DESTRUCTION. Staging bytes before Evidence creation use `temporary_processing`; Verification challenge plaintext remains `ephemeral_secret` and is never part of Evidence. Payload expiry is exactly 24 months on the capture cursor; the 30-day warning precedes it. A legal hold suspends destruction and the payload is destroyed at the first eligible instant after release. The window values are owned by 015 DATA_LIFECYCLE.md; this row restates only what CAP-013 and its resolved decisions make behavioural.

MTX-013.rollout: S-11 depends on S-08 for the producer contracts and on S-09 for the Check Results whose frozen Decision tuples it must never rewrite; it gates S-12 (Issue Evidence integrity), S-13 (score availability) and S-14 (Artifact suppression and republication). MTX-067.interface_type: Complete-contract and propagation rule for Evidence. PRULE-016 governs CAP-013, CAP-015 and CAP-016 and applies to WF-003, WF-006, WF-007, WF-008, WF-009 and WF-013. This row owns the rule for S-11, S-13 and S-14; S-13 consumes its score-unavailability limb and S-14 its Artifact-suppression limb, and neither re-contracts it. Its decision dependencies OD-011, OD-029 and OD-030 are all RESOLVED; nothing here is withheld.
MTX-067.route: Not applicable - PRULE-016 is a rule, not an interface.
MTX-067.request_schema: Not applicable - constrains the MTX-013 schema and the producer contracts owned by S-05 and S-08.
MTX-067.command: Enforced at every Evidence creation performed by a producing workflow, within `Workflows::Wf007::SubmitEvidenceValidationDecision`, and as a precondition on every downstream Issue, Score Contribution, Recommendation Artifact and Citation write. This row adds no command.
MTX-067.command_input: Not applicable - constrains the MTX-013 input.
MTX-067.command_output: Not applicable - constrains the MTX-013 output.
MTX-067.actor: The producing workflow's service identity at creation; the integrity-validation service and, for quarantine only, a scoped SecurityOperator at transition. The rule constrains the record and the propagation, not a principal.
MTX-067.organization_scope: The Evidence's Organization; the same-Organization clause is part of the rule's own text.
MTX-067.aggregate: Evidence and EvidenceValidationDecision as the constrained roots; CurrentScoreProjection, ScoreSnapshot, RecommendationArtifact and Citation as propagation targets.
MTX-067.aggregate_boundary: The rule's atomicity clause is what makes the propagation commit wide rather than eventual: expiry, hold or another effective transition away from valid MUST atomically make affected current score and recommendation projections unavailable or suppressed WITHOUT rewriting history. Both halves are load-bearing -- a narrow commit leaves a stale numeric score readable, and a history-rewriting commit destroys the immutable snapshot the product's explainability rests on.
MTX-067.value_objects: ValidationStatus, EvidenceValidationDecisionId, DataClassification, PayloadRetentionClass, ProductHistoryClass, ContentSha256, EvidenceProvenance, UnavailableReasonCode, PublicationStatus.
MTX-067.domain_service: Not applicable - PRULE-016 names no domain service; the tenant-scoped integrity-validation service it relies on is named by CAP-013 and contracted in MTX-013.
MTX-067.persistence_model: Not applicable as a new concept - PRULE-016 introduces no record. It makes the complete Evidence field, digest, provenance, validation, classification, immutability and same-Organization contract mandatory before downstream use, and it fixes the retention split at the column level: only `payload_retention_class` on the referenced Payload is `product_evidence_payload`; the envelope and lineage are `product_history` and retain after payload destruction.
MTX-067.migration: Not applicable - no schema object is added; this row requires no canonical namespace for an unassigned record, so the OD-032 limb withheld on MTX-013 does not reach it.
MTX-067.transaction_boundary: As MTX-013 - one transaction per Decision performing every applicable current effect before commit and enqueuing idempotent recalculation. The rule's contribution is that the transaction is mandatory and its scope is exhaustive, not that it introduces a new boundary.
MTX-067.concurrency: The mandatory expected validation-state version prevents two concurrent transitions on one Evidence record. Because history is never rewritten, a concurrent historical read is unaffected by an in-flight transition: it reads the frozen state-at-snapshot values.
MTX-067.idempotency: The Decision replay contract is the rule's idempotency guarantee: exact replay returns the Decision without repeating suppression, the event or recalculation. Recalculation is itself idempotent and replaces the complete reason set rather than applying a delta, so a redelivery converges to the same reason set instead of accumulating codes.
MTX-067.background_job: Not applicable - the rule constrains a synchronous commit and the recalculation it enqueues; it defines no job of its own. The retention-expiry and destruction jobs are MTX-013's.
MTX-067.queue: Not applicable - no queue of its own.
MTX-067.retry_policy: Not applicable - PRULE-016 defines no retry. A rejected creation or Decision is not retried; the correct recovery is new Evidence or a new Decision against the latest version.
MTX-067.terminal_failure: Evidence failing the complete contract has NO downstream use: it supports no Issue, no included Score Contribution, no Recommendation Artifact and no customer-visible citation. `invalid` is terminal. The rule fails downstream writes closed rather than degrading them.
MTX-067.reconciliation: History is never rewritten. Historical views reconstruct Issue and adjudication state only from each ScoreSnapshot's immutable Contributions, including captured Issue state version, lifecycle, publication and adjudication values, Case references, Evidence IDs and Validation Decision IDs and statuses. Current views use the Current Score Projection and return no numeric score while it is unavailable, even though the retained last snapshot remains accessible AS HISTORY. That separation is the reconciliation: the same Evidence transition makes the current view unavailable and leaves the historical view intact.
MTX-067.domain_events: Not applicable - PRULE-016 emits no event of its own; it gates `EvidenceValidationChanged` and `EvidenceRetentionExpiring`, which MTX-013 emits, and it is why a suppression is committed before, not after, the event.
